mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of RSAFS growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of UNRATE decrease (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of INDPRO increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% each within the last two months signals a strong demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS increase > 5% each in 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of joint HOUST and RSAFS increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals deflationary pressure, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of CPIAUCSL decrease (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% each within the last month signals a tightening labor market with increased employment, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 0.5% and UNRATE decrease > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: labor market tightening with employment growth
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of joint PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of GDPC1 growth (t-test p > 0.05).
